import math
# Percentage increases
new_haven = 69/399
hartford = 117/629

print(f'New Haven % increase: {new_haven}')
print(f'Hartford % increase: {hartford}')

# Normalize to create distributions
total = new_haven + hartford
P = [new_haven/total, hartford/total]
Q = [hartford/total, new_haven/total]

print(f'P = {P}')
print(f'Q = {Q}')

# KL divergence D_KL(P||Q)
kl = P[0] * math.log(P[0]/Q[0]) + P[1] * math.log(P[1]/Q[1])
print(f'D_KL(P||Q) = {kl}')

# Alternative: symmetric version (average of both directions)
kl_reverse = Q[0] * math.log(Q[0]/P[0]) + Q[1] * math.log(Q[1]/P[1])
print(f'D_KL(Q||P) = {kl_reverse}')
print(f'Average = {(kl + kl_reverse)/2}')
"

import math
# Percentage increases (from the data)
new_haven_pct = 69/399
hartford_pct = 117/629

# Normalize to create the two point distributions
total = new_haven_pct + hartford_pct

# Distribution P: New Haven first, then Hartford (normalized)
P_new_haven = new_haven_pct / total
P_hartford = hartford_pct / total

# Distribution Q: Hartford first (reversed order), then New Haven (normalized)
Q_hartford = hartford_pct / total
Q_new_haven = new_haven_pct / total

# KL divergence D_KL(P||Q)
# P = [P_new_haven, P_hartford]
# Q = [Q_hartford, Q_new_haven]
# Since Q_hartford = P_hartford and Q_new_haven = P_new_haven, they're swapped

kl_divergence = P_new_haven * math.log(P_new_haven / Q_hartford) + P_hartford * math.log(P_hartford / Q_new_haven)

print(f'Percentage increase New Haven: {new_haven_pct:.10f}')
print(f'Percentage increase Hartford: {hartford_pct:.10f}')
print(f'P = [{P_new_haven:.10f}, {P_hartford:.10f}]')
print(f'Q = [{Q_hartford:.10f}, {Q_new_haven:.10f}]')
print(f'KL Divergence = {kl_divergence:.10f}')
print(f'KL Divergence (5 decimal places) = {kl_divergence:.5f}')
"
